text: SUCH IS FAME.

label: text
text:
MATINEE IDOL'S SUCCESS
LOCALLY.

label: text
text: SEQUEL TO STRIKE.

label: text
text: Mr. Sit Kok-seen, the famous Cantonese matinee idol, who is the first "star" to perform in Hongkong since the strike began last year, has been playing to capacity houses this week. The attendance was such that queues lined up each night at the Kau-U Fong theatre and seats were booked up several nights ahead. Many had to be turned away.

label: text
text: When the strike began last year, all the leading troupes returned to Canton. Subsequently shows were given by amateur companies and by smaller troupes who got through or were assembled from other sources.

label: text
text: Mr. Sit (better known as Mr. S. C. Harrey) has been in Shanghai for over a year, where he holds the position of managing director of the Ideal Motion Film Co., He is on a short business trip to Hongkong. Starting as an amateur actor a few years ago, he rose very quickly to the top and his career has been meteoric.

label: text
text: Other "stars" have come to Hongkong, but only to sail for America, where there are several Cantonese companies. The cutting out of the Hongkong and Macao theatres from the itinerary of the Cantonese troupes has meant a fairly big exodus to America, and Malaya. Mr. Sit Kok-seen is the first actually to appear on a Hongkong stage since last June, except for a former colleague who appeared in charity shows here, while awaiting a steamer for Seattle.

label: paragraph_title
text: IDLE RICH.

label: text
text: MUSSOINI CLASSES THEM WITH TRAMPS.

label: text
text: IN ROLE OF OUTCASTS

label: text
text:
Signor Mussolini has declared
who on the idle rich, who are included in the same classification
as beggars and tramps in the new
grouping system for electoral and industrial purposes of the whole
Italian nation, which will be
effected by legislation expected to
come into force on July 1.

label: text
text: Unproductive, rich, vagabonds, and tramps will be excluded under this system from the benefits of Italian citizenship.

label: text
text:
Italians will be grouped into fifteen categories. The sections of industry, sea transport, commerce, agriculture, land transport, and banking are further subdivided into employers and employees' groups, making twelve categories in all. There are also three more groups of independent workers, neither employers nor employees, such as doctors, lawyers, artists, and engineers.
The classification of the idle rich with beggars and tramps has created much indignant comfort. Signor Muissolini, however, has often expressed his contempt for idlers, and a law against voluntary parasitism will, no doubt, be promulgated shortly.

label: text
text: All non-producers are to live “on the margin of the State,” that is, they will be treated as foreigners, not as Italian citizens.

label: paragraph_title
text: SENSIBLE TYPISTS.

label: text
text:
HAPPIER THAN £10-A-WEEK
AMERICANS.

label: text
text: Southampton, June 25.

label: text
text: Mr. Roy S. Wildman, whose copper mills in America employ 35,000 men, dispelled some of the dreams about his country as the workers' utopia of high wages, when interviewed to-day before he sailed for New York.

label: text
text: "Shorthand-typists in America," he said, "earn from £6 to £10 a week, but the cost of living is proportionately high. They are no happier than their less-paid sisters in England, because in their feverish anxiety to maintain the standard of living they set themselves they are able to put only a little money in the bank."

label: text
text: "The craze for dress, which is the result of high wages, attains ridiculous heights. Shorthand-typists earning good money in New York and other great cities arrive at their offices dressed like revue stars. The English office girl's attire is much more sensible than that of the American girl."

label: paragraph_title
text: COMRADE KOPP.

label: text
text: ARRIVED IN MOSCOW SAYS DEVELOPMENT NORMAL.

label: paragraph_title
text: JAPANESE-SOVIET RELATIONS.

label: text
text: Moscow, July 24.—In an interview with the press men shortly after his arrival here from Japan, Mr. Victor Kopp, the Soviet Ambassador to Tokyo, who is home on furlough, emphasised the normal development of Japanese-Soviet relations.

label: text
text: In illustration, he pointed to the successful settlement of a number of different questions, specifying the Soviet-Japanese agreement on Saghallen concessions among the successes and also predicting in the very near future the conclusion of a Fishery Convention between the two countries.

label: text
text: Mr. Kopp also insisted on the evidence of development of commercial relations between the Russian Republic and Japan since the installation of the Russian trade delegation at Tokyo and said he had been informed that before long there would be started parleys with representatives of the South Manchuria Railway, the Chinese Eastern Railway and with the Ussuri Railway for the regulation of railway traffic and construction in Manchuria.

label: text
text: The village of Quarto Disoecavo, near Naples, is much excited over what they regard as the treatment of diseases by a local priest, Don Luigi Garofalo.

label: text
text: More than a hundred cases ranging from tuberculosis to paralysis and from toothache to broken limbs, are stated to have been treated successfully by this prior with a special earth found near Pozzuoli (on the coast near Naples). The earth is either taken in the form of pills or applied externally to the injured part.

label: text
text: The prigst's fame has spread rapidly throughout the province and his house has become the object of numerous pilgrimages by people suffering from all sorts of diseases.

label: paragraph_title
text: CHOLERA IN SHANGHAI.

label: text
text: The Chinese community of Chapei and Nantao is seriously alarmed at the rapid spread of the cholera epidemic. In a further petition to Dr. V. K. Ting on the subject, the Chinese merchants state that so long as the working classes are allowed to use creek water for cooking and drinking, the epidemic will continue. The petition states that the workers of innumerable cotton factories and silk flatures on the Chinese side of the "Soochow Creek" use water direct from the creek for all domestic purposes, including drinking. The petition adds that the factory management should be compelled to have sanitary wells dug. Dr. Ting has issued further orders in connection with the epidemic, and these, he says, must be obeyed. It is his stated intention to walk through the streets himself during the nights to see that the police obey his instructions and prevent the people from sleeping in the open. The regulations regarding the sale of unclean food must be tightened, and most important of all, corpses must be immediately buried, and not allowed to lie in the homes in accordance with ancient Chinese customs. Dr. Ting regards this particular custom as an especial evil.
